meta_title: Linux Requirements of VpnHood! CLIENT and CONNECT | VpnHood!
meta_description: The Linux distributions VpnHood! CLIENT and VpnHood! CONNECT run on, the processor they need, and what the system needs for DNS, QUIC and the kill switch.
title: Linux requirements
lead: Check your Linux machine before you install VpnHood! CLIENT or VpnHood! CONNECT: its distribution, its processor and, above all, a way to set the VPN's DNS. Without it, the app cannot connect.
system_desc: The apps run on x64 and ARM64. They install and start on these distributions; the ones built on them, and others with systemd and glibc, should also work:
unsupported: Not supported: Alpine and the other distributions built on musl instead of glibc. The installer finishes there, but the app cannot start.
need_root: Root access to install the app, and systemd, which runs its VPN service.
need_admin: An administrator's account to use it: root, or a member of the [group_sudo], [group_wheel] or [group_admin] group. A line in the sudoers file is not enough.
need_tun: A TUN device for the VPN, which nearly every machine has.
need_dns: A way to set the VPN's DNS: [pkg_resolved], turned on, or [pkg_resolvconf]. Without one, the app cannot connect, and its error says what to do. Many systems have [pkg_resolved] turned off, so check this first.
need_nft: For the kill switch, [pkg_nftables], which the installer adds, and cgroup v2. Without them, the app says so and does not connect while the kill switch is on.
need_quic: For QUIC, MsQuic, which the installer adds. Where it cannot, as on Amazon Linux 2023, the app connects without QUIC.
need_desktop: For the window, a desktop. The installer adds the libraries the window needs. Without a desktop, you get the VPN service and the commands.
need_connect: VpnHood! CONNECT signs in from its window, so for now it needs a desktop.
